clue.text: Mark equivalent 'to 50 centavos?

definitions.meaning: a punctuation mark, the stop between a comma and a full stop in weight
the colón of Costa Rica and El Salvador is worth 100 centavos, so half of one, a semi-colón, is 50

explanation.surface: Someone asks what mark of currency matches fifty Latin American centavos.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: the second reading splits the word into SEMI (half) and COLON, the Central American currency unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation symbol ; is a mark used in writing between clauses.

clue.text: Part of letter lights up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: lights as a verb means fires, sets alight

explanation.surface: A section of a written letter brightens up.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small stroke finishing part of a printed letter.

clue.text: In the coal industry, a companion is operating the plant

indicators.note: the article and companion go inside the industry word

parts.note: coal is dug out by mining
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A colleague runs the machinery at a coal pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts the pieces inside the industry word just after its first letter. The Companion of Honour is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Machining is working with machine tools, so running the plant.

clue.text: The snag people found over time collecting water

indicators.note: in a down clue, the people sit above the time letter

parts.note: a catch is a hidden snag or drawback
men means people

explanation.surface: People discover the hitch, a delay with water collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchment is an area or system that gathers rainwater draining into a river or reservoir.

clue.text: It could be lovely if they all made a bloomer

indicators.note: these words could be rearranged into another phrase

explanation.surface: Something lovely could result if everyone made a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' seems to mean a blunder, but it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a plant that flowers, and this is a spring woodland flower.

clue.text: Cry and beef about love and cordiality

parts.note: a neigh is a horse's cry

indicators.note: the strength word goes round the letter for love

parts.note: beef means brawn, burliness
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Someone shouts and complains about romance and warm friendliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like a grumble but is muscle, BURLINESS, round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Being friendly and helpful to those nearby is a form of cordiality.

clue.text: A bit of a fight

definitions.meaning: an informal word for a brawl or scuffle

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday nouns: a tiny leftover piece, and a minor punch-up.

clue.text: Son' without means to follow track

indicators.note: the poverty word comes after the son's letter

parts.note: poor means without money

explanation.surface: A penniless son goes off to follow a path.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the trail or tracks left by an animal.

clue.text: Leaders in rural area discuss innovative ideas — more than one spoke

indicators.note: the leading letters of the following words are picked

explanation.surface: Rural community heads hold talks on new ideas, and several speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoke' looks like the past of speak, but is a wheel's rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Radii are the spokes of a wheel, plural of radius.

clue.text: Missing nothing, unfortunate dog's seen shark

indicators.note: the zero letter is absent from the word

parts.note: poor means unlucky or unfortunate
O is zero, nothing
a beagle is a breed of hound

explanation.surface: An unlucky dog, lost and unaccounted for, spots a shark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing' removes an O from POOR, leaving POR.
explanation.definitionFit: The porbeagle is a large species of mackerel shark.

clue.text: Account given in rewritten article

indicators.note: something rewritten has had its contents rearranged, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A report appears inside a newspaper piece that has been revised.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a detailed narration or account of events, as in a recital of grievances.

clue.text: Monk is working

definitions.meaning: a monk belongs to a religious order, so is someone in one
a machine that is functioning properly is in good order

explanation.definitionFit: A monk is a member of a religious order; a machine fit to run is said to be functional.

clue.text: Trust I put in pop, with no sign of hesitation

indicators.note: the letter I is placed inside what remains of the word for pop
the hesitation sound is removed from the word for pop

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
ER is the sound a speaker makes when hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone puts their trust in their dad, now speaking without stammering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' strips the hesitation sound from pop's word, leaving FATH; 'put in' then places I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Faith is firm trust or confidence in someone or something.

clue.text: Old king surrounded by those who are shrewd in a different way

indicators.note: the king's letter is enclosed within the phrase for the shrewd people

parts.note: the wise are those who are shrewd
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch finds himself encircled by clever advisers who see things differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise is an adverb meaning differently or in another manner.

clue.text: Man in church might produce this

definitions.text: Man in church might produce this

indicators.note: the word for man is placed inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
him is a pronoun standing for a man

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer in a church tower might make this sound.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue pictures a bell-ringer in a church tower making a peal; read as wordplay, 'in' sets the pronoun inside the church's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chime is the ringing sound of bells, which a man in a church tower makes.

clue.text: I can't shop if this is out of order

definitions.text: I can't shop if this is out of order

indicators.note: letters out of order are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopper laments that the broken cash machine stops them buying.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue is a shopper's complaint about a broken cash machine; 'out of order' also scrambles the first three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A cashpoint is a cash machine; without it working one cannot get money to shop.

clue.text: Getting walkover in several races, I am in good form, cheating

indicators.note: the walkover abbreviation goes inside the races abbreviation

parts.note: the TT races are the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle races
WO is the abbreviation for walkover, a win without a contest
contracted to I'm
taken as written

explanation.surface: A racer boasts of easy wins in several events and fine form while being unfaithful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting' and 'form' are surface padding; the TT is a famous series of motorcycle races on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-timing means deceiving a partner by secretly seeing someone else, a kind of cheating.

clue.text: Sauce? Popular fish enjoyable without one

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
sole is a flatfish

indicators.note: the letter for one is removed

parts.note: nice means pleasant or enjoyable
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A menu asks for a sauce for a favourite fish, which tastes good without it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' looks like food, but means cheek; 'without' removes I from NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce is informal for cheeky rudeness, which is insolence.

clue.text: City in which I condemn/a criminal

parts.note: to slam is to criticise or condemn harshly
bad means wicked or criminal

explanation.surface: Someone in a city denounces a wrongdoer.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamabad is the capital city of Pakistan.

clue.text: Tourist displaying tigers he's shot

indicators.note: shot as in wrecked or ruined, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A traveller on safari shows off the tigers he has shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like hunting, but means broken up: rearrange TIGERSHES.
explanation.definitionFit: A sightseer is a tourist visiting the notable sights of a place.

clue.text: One divided by five — work out the answer

indicators.note: the word for one is split apart by the Roman numeral

parts.note: sole means only or single, one alone
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A maths student is told to calculate one over five.
explanation.definitionFit: To solve a problem is to find or work out its answer.

clue.text: Almost go to pieces carrying a coffin from 16, perhaps

indicators.note: the shortened word holds the next pieces inside it
the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to panic is to lose control and go to pieces
kist is a Scots and northern word for a chest or coffin

explanation.surface: Someone nearly breaks down while bearing a coffin at a funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the panicking word to PANI, which 'carrying' wraps round the rest. Entry 16 is ISLAMABAD, so someone from there may be the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Islamabad, the national capital, would be a citizen of that country.

clue.text: King and ace laid down, not 10

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in cards and chess
put means placed or laid down

explanation.surface: A card player lays down king and ace, but not the ten.
explanation.walkthrough: Entry 10 is IN ORDER, meaning working; the answer means broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaput means broken, not working, the opposite of functioning properly.

clue.text: Doctor not on the crest of a wave

indicators.note: the word on is taken away

parts.note: a surgeon is a kind of doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor is not riding high on success.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a powerful rising swell, the peak movement of the sea.

clue.text: Road having lights all round — speed restriction applied

indicators.note: the word for lights wraps entirely round the road

parts.note: lit means lights, as in sets alight or illuminates
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, often written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A road lined with street lamps has a speed cap imposed on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a major British motorway, written MI here.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed limit is a legal restriction on how fast one may drive.

clue.text: Very small target near city

indicators.note: the city's letters come right beside the target

parts.note: the tee is the target in curling and quoits
NY is New York

explanation.surface: A tiny target lies close to a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeny is informal for tiny or very small.

clue.text: Sovereign, dismissing army leader, is put in danger

indicators.note: the leader's letter is sent away from the longer word

parts.note: imperial means sovereign, relating to an emperor

indicators.note: the first letter of army leads it

explanation.surface: A monarch, sacking his chief general, finds himself in jeopardy.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil is to endanger or expose to risk.

clue.text: Raise capital, once back in the Spanish quarter

indicators.note: the reversed city goes into the Spanish article

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: the old capital's name is read backwards

parts.note: Bonn was the capital of West Germany
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A Spanish district helps fund a former capital's revival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the former West German capital's name, and 'in' places the result inside the Spanish article before the compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise someone to the nobility or to a higher dignity.

clue.text: It's included in the financial contribution

indicators.note: the pronoun is placed within the article

parts.note: taken as written, the 's a link meaning is

explanation.surface: A note explains that something is covered in a payment made.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe is a tenth of income given as a contribution to the church.

clue.text: In the past, you once strayed disastrously

parts.note: ye is the archaic form of you

indicators.note: a disaster turns things upside down, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recalls how you previously went badly off course.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterday is used figuratively to mean in the recent past.
